learning.title: A JSX space between an inline-flex link's text and its icon renders as nothing; the gap belongs on the variant
learning.trigger: An arrow or icon inside an inline-flex link sits flush against its text; or a spacing attempt between the text and the icon has no visible effect in the browser or in a visual capture; or a link that must sit inside a sentence jumps onto a line of its own with a gap above it.
learning.mistake: Left a whitespace expression between the text and the icon and expected it to render, then chased the missing space as a font, token or padding problem.
learning.rule: `.ui-link`'s base is `display: inline-flex; align-items: center` with no gap (packages/ui/src/controls.css:17-20), and that one declaration causes two distinct bugs. (1) The container collapses the whitespace-only text nodes between its children, so a JSX space between an inline-flex link's text and its glyph is dead on arrival: the space belongs in CSS, as `gap` on the variant that carries the glyph — `.ui-link--quiet { gap: var(--space-1) }`, landed in bb4cdf918 (#482), whose commit message records that it also cleared the four quiet links in IssuePage.tsx. (2) An inline-flex link cannot sit inside a sentence without being pushed onto a line of its own with a gap above it, so that case needs a variant of its own: `.ui-link--sentence { display: inline; min-block-size: 0 }` (controls.css:122-125, #475). Both were fixed at the variant, never at a call site, which is the part to carry: when one link's spacing or wrapping looks wrong, read the shared variant before touching the instance, and check which manifestation you have before choosing display or gap.

verification.requirement: Read the tracked file, not the working tree: the primary clone lags origin/main, so a stale checkout makes a landed rule look absent. Then confirm the space comes from a gap on the variant — or the wrapping from its display — and prove it with the story check and a visual capture at the head SHA.
